clue.text: Adult males, competent and likely to cooperate

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
males are men
competent means capable

explanation.surface: A description of grown men who are capable and willing to work together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is open and responsive to suggestion, so ready to go along with others.

clue.text: Full of admiration for a bridge player at a gathering of players

parts.note: taken as written
North, South, East and West are the four players at a bridge table
in rugby a ruck is a loose cluster of players over the ball

explanation.surface: Someone admires a card player at a club meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruck is a rugby term: players from both sides bunch over a ball on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To be awestruck is to be overcome with wonder and reverence, close kin to great admiration.

clue.text: Berlin song — none better broadcast so far inside

indicators.note: something lying far inside is placed deep within the other letters
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
so and as are interchangeable in comparisons, as in 'not so good as'

explanation.surface: A boast that no song by Irving Berlin has yet been better aired on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin's song Easter Parade opens with the line 'In your Easter bonnet', which the clue takes as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyric about a festive spring hat is the famous opening of a song written by Irving Berlin.

clue.text: See 1
Partly describe an office party

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters straddling them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a brief account of a workplace celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office party' reads as one phrase, but office only lends its first letter and party is the definition. A beano is British slang for a lively celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a festive gathering or knees-up, the same thing as a party.

clue.text: It's edible and good aboard coaster at sea

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vessel is carried inside it
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the vessel the letter boards
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Praise for the food served on a small coastal ship at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An escargot is a snail cooked as a delicacy, so the vague 'it's edible' fits it.

clue.text: Always effective for all to see, aboard ferries at sea

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a boat sits inside it
at sea means muddled and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the vessels the letter boards
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Something reliably works on cross-channel boats for everyone to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating 'universal', a film fit for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A sure-fire method is certain to succeed, one that never fails to work.

clue.text: See 6
Lumber theologian put in auction

indicators.note: to be put in something is to be placed inside it

parts.note: an auction is a sale
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Old timber and a scholar of religion are both offered under the hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lumber here is the verb 'burden', not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To lumber someone with a task is to burden them, the same as to saddle them with it.

clue.text: All that is in revues (edited)

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that everything has been cut into the theatre shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All that is in' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the totality of existence, everything there is.

clue.text: Girl caught in grip of another

indicators.note: something in the grip of another is held enclosed by it

parts.note: another girl's name
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: One girl is seized and held by a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second girl's name, carrying on from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcia is a female first name, so it suits the general word for a young woman.

clue.text: Novel move by armada at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh tactic by a fleet of warships out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel move' reads as 'new manoeuvre'; Novel is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is Flaubert's famous 1857 work of fiction.

clue.text: Result — level at end of contest

parts.note: level means even

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of contest

explanation.surface: A match ends all square in the final reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or consequence can be called an event, as in 'in the event'.

clue.text: Smitten girl wore black, burying knight

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

indicators.note: what is buried is put out of sight, so that letter disappears from the word

parts.note: people in mourning traditionally wear black
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A girl dressed in black at the funeral of a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The buried knight is removed from the mourning word rather than hidden inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enamoured is to be in love, just as smitten means struck with infatuation.

clue.text: Hypocritical show of affection in press coming to nothing

parts.note: a press is a cupboard, as in a linen press
love means nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Insincere affection reported in the newspapers turns out to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like the newspapers, but it is the old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is fondness shown only for what one can get, like a pet fawning for food.

clue.text: Cast doubt on record? Tried, stupidly

indicators.note: done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so the letters come out disordered

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
the letters of tried rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone questions a record attempt made foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit something is to make it doubted or disbelieved.

clue.text: Improved the appearance of pad? Utter nonsense

indicators.note: nonsense is senseless jumble, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneer at someone who claims to have made a flat look nicer.
explanation.walkthrough: Utter looks like a verb or an intensifier for nonsense, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To tart something up is British slang for smartening or decorating it, often cheaply.

clue.text: Gift from boy — perfume?

parts.note: Frank is a boy's name
incense is a fragrance that is burnt

explanation.surface: A present from a lad, and the question is whether it is scent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the Nativity: frankincense was one of the three gifts of the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense was one of the presents the wise men brought to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: This kind of music is fun, dancing, holding love

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places
holding something means keeping it inside

parts.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A happy claim that this music is a joy to move to, with romance in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fun' reads as part of the sentence's verb phrase but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusion is a musical genre blending styles, most often jazz with rock or funk.

clue.text: Ignite sack during argument

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within its span

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or scrap
to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed in the middle of a row and tempers flare.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to start it burning.

clue.text: Angry in lift, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to lift is to steal or copy, which is to pirate

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in an elevator loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift suggests an elevator, but it means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a straightforward synonym for furious or angry.

clue.text: Drive back from dance bypassing centre of Memphis

indicators.note: a road bypassing a town goes round it, so the dance wraps around the letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A dance tour avoids the heart of the Tennessee city.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to force them back.

clue.text: Box hidden in tree in London street

indicators.note: something hidden in another is tucked away inside it

parts.note: the plane is a common tree in London streets
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A box has been stashed in a tree on a city road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' suggests the answer is spelt out inside the clue, but it is a container signal. Park Lane runs along Hyde Park and is the priciest square on the British Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: Park Lane is a famous road in the Mayfair district of central London.

clue.text: See 21
Tediously familiar lot had dispersed

indicators.note: a dispersed crowd breaks up and scatters, so the letters do too

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boring, predictable crowd that has already gone home.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale and unoriginal because seen too often.

clue.text: Foremost of societies, together with Press Club

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of societies
and means together with
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A leading society teams up with a club for journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press Club' reads as a journalists' club, but Club alone is the definition, a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand iron is a golf club, the old name for the sand wedge used in bunkers.

clue.text: Ibsen drama exercises gentry, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
the letters of gentry rearranged

explanation.surface: A Norwegian play unexpectedly puts the upper classes through their paces.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is Henrik Ibsen's 1867 verse play about a roguish Norwegian wanderer.
